- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to rise gradually but overshoot true values after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 34.62 → 35.94 → 35.70).
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after a spike, forecast declines too slowly or fails to correct downward.
- Forecast horizon (30d) shows persistent lag: true values often dip below forecast mid-period, then recover — model fails to capture this reversal.
- Model underreacts to low historical prices (e.g., 31.73, 31.63) — forecasts remain elevated instead of adjusting downward.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture volatility or sudden drops in true outcomes (e.g., 35.94 → 34.01 → 32.75).
- Model tends to overcorrect after a low, then overshoots again — creates “double dip” pattern in forecast vs true.
- Forecasts often peak too early and then plateau — fails to reflect true price volatility or policy-driven corrections.
- Model ignores recent low prices in history when forecasting — fails to adjust downward when true values dip below 33.00.
